subject: green heron
title: This Bird Goes Fishing With Bait: Bread, Bugs, Even Feathers

scenes.text: This bird goes fishing with bait.
The green heron is a small heron that crouches at the water's edge, waiting.
Sometimes it brings something along: a bread crust, an insect, a feather.
It drops the lure on the surface, freezes, and watches.
Small fish swim up to nibble. The heron snatches them with its dagger of a bill.
That makes it one of the very few birds on Earth that use tools. And it fishes the way you do.

description:
The green heron catches fish by setting out bait.
According to the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, green herons make fishing lures from bread crusts, insects and feathers, dropping them on the water to entice small fish, which makes the species one of the world's few tool-using birds. Twigs work too: the heron drops one, freezes, lets it attract a minnow, then strikes with its daggerlike bill. Most of the time it simply hunts by sitting and waiting at the edge of ponds, marshes and streams.
Have you ever seen a bird do something this clever? Comment below.
first_comment: A few other herons and egrets have been seen bait-fishing too, some with bread people threw to ducks. Have you ever seen a bird do something this clever?
